Container.Name: tape
Container.Overview: Tape — Schwab-backed market + account data tier for CEF Tracker + Keystone. ONE neutral template for dev and prod: at creation set Name (tape / tape-dev), image tag (:stable for prod, :dev for dev), network + a static IP if you use one, and the discrete DB_* vars pointing at the tape-db container. The app assembles the DB connection string from DB_HOST/DB_PORT/DB_USER/DB_PASSWORD/DB_NAME (§2 B.10) — no baked DATABASE_URL. Everything else (SCHWAB_CALLBACK_URL and ~87 other settings) is database-managed via the admin API, seeded with shipped defaults — see the header comment.
Container.Description: Tape — Schwab-backed market + account data tier (one neutral template, dev+prod).

Config.Name: HTTP Port
Config.Description: App HTTP port

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Encrypted token store. REQUIRED - set an absolute path on a POOL (e.g. /mnt/<pool>/appdata/tape/data, or .../tape-dev/data for a dev container). Do NOT leave it blank and do not point it at the RAM-backed root filesystem. The retrievable ops/error logs also default to a subdirectory of this mount.

Config.Name: Backups
Config.Description: Where the scheduled pg_dump lands. REQUIRED for a real backup: WITHOUT this mount the dump is written INSIDE the container and destroyed by the next update — the job still reports success, which is why it went unnoticed for months. Set an absolute path on a POOL DIFFERENT from the one holding the DB container's data (e.g. /mnt/<other-pool>/appdata/tape/backups), so one pool failure cannot take both the warehouse and its only backup. The app WARNS (ntfy) at boot and at every dump if this path is not a persistent mount. ⚠️ THIS MOUNT IS THE BACKUP_DIR SETTING — there is deliberately no BACKUP_DIR Variable, because the two must never disagree: a Variable pointing anywhere other than this mount point would send dumps into the container filesystem, which is the exact silent failure above.

Config.Name: Shared alerting config
Config.Description: READ-ONLY mount of the shared fleet config directory — set the host path to the directory holding configs/alerting.env (EMAIL_TO, EMAIL_FROM, SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASSWORD, and the ntfy topics NTFY_URL_TAPE / NTFY_URL_DEV / NTFY_URL_PROD). THIS MOUNT IS BOTH ALERT CHANNELS, ntfy AND email: both are deliberately read from that file at send time and NEVER from a per-container environment variable, because an environment variable is visible to anyone who can run a container inspect and both an SMTP password and an ntfy topic are real credentials. SHARED_ROOT below must point at wherever this mount lands INSIDE the container. Without this mount both channels are unreachable and every alert this service raises goes NOWHERE (it says so loudly in the boot log). One file serves the whole fleet, so rotating the password, moving the inbox or repointing a topic is one edit rather than one per container.

Config.Name: SCHWAB_APP_KEY
Config.Description: Schwab app key

Config.Name: SCHWAB_APP_SECRET
Config.Description: Schwab app secret

Config.Name: TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY
Config.Description: Fernet key for token-at-rest encryption

Config.Name: DB_HOST
Config.Description: Warehouse DB host - the address of the tape-db container serving THIS environment

Config.Name: DB_PORT
Config.Description: Warehouse DB port

Config.Name: DB_USER
Config.Description: Warehouse DB user (matches the tape-db container's POSTGRES_USER)

Config.Name: DB_PASSWORD
Config.Description: Warehouse DB password (matches the tape-db container's POSTGRES_PASSWORD)

Config.Name: DB_NAME
Config.Description: Warehouse DB name (matches the tape-db container's POSTGRES_DB)

Config.Name: DATABASE_URL
Config.Description: OPTIONAL override — full SQLAlchemy URL (postgresql+psycopg://user:pass@host:port/db). Leave BLANK to use the discrete DB_* vars above; if set, it wins.

Config.Name: DEPLOY_ENV
Config.Description: REQUIRED - type prod or dev. It selects which shared ntfy topic this container falls back to when NTFY_URL_TAPE is not set (NTFY_URL_PROD or NTFY_URL_DEV) and which keys the shared file must carry. DELIBERATELY BLANK: a default here would silently put a dev deployment on the prod topic, and the symptom of that is an incident that paged the wrong place. Case does not matter.

Config.Name: SHARED_ROOT
Config.Description: The CONTAINER path the Shared alerting config mount above is mounted at. Leave it alone - it must match that mount's container-side target, and the operator chooses only the HOST side. Change both together or neither.

Config.Name: CONFIG_PATH
Config.Description: A directory this container owns and writes, holding one small marker file that records which alerting config it last validated — which is what makes the one-time validation alert fire on a config change rather than on every restart. Defaults to a subdirectory of the Data mount above so there is no second volume to get wrong.

Config.Name: B2_KEY_ID
Config.Description: Backblaze B2 key id, for the optional built-in offsite leg. See B2_BUCKET — normally blank.

Config.Name: B2_APPLICATION_KEY
Config.Description: Backblaze B2 application key, for the optional built-in offsite leg. See B2_BUCKET — normally blank.

Config.Name: SCHEDULER_ENABLED
Config.Description: Master switch for ALL recurring work — the daily cycle, every feed, the backups, and every watchdog. False leaves the API serving reads while nothing maintains the warehouse; useful for a second read-only instance, dangerous as a default. ⭐ LEAVE THIS BLANK unless you mean to override it. Blank means ON, which is what Tape ships. Unlike every other Variable in this section this one has NO row in job_schedules — it is the master switch rather than a schedule, so blank falls through to the shipped default rather than to a stored row. Set it to false only to run an instance that serves reads and maintains nothing. GET /v1/admin/scheduler reports whether it is in force.

Config.Name: FRED_API_KEY
Config.Description: FRED (St. Louis Fed) API key — free from fred.stlouisfed.org (32 alphanumeric). Enables the macro feed (yield curve, rates, spreads, inflation, dollar index). Unset = the FRED job no-ops; the rest of Tape is unaffected. Whether the feed runs at all, its schedule, and every other feed tuning knob are now database-managed (job_schedules/app_config) — set FRED_ENABLED etc. via the admin API if you need to change them from the shipped defaults.

Config.Name: TIINGO_API_TOKEN
Config.Description: OPTIONAL personal API token for the higher-quality alternate price source (free tier at tiingo.com). Tape repairs a missing daily bar from alternate sources when the primary feed is asked for that session and returns nothing; two keyless sources are tried first, and this one is tried only for what they could not serve, so a personal quota is spent on the remainder rather than the whole universe. Leave BLANK and that lane is completely dormant — no request is made, nothing is logged, and the free lanes do all the work. Unset is a fully supported configuration, not a degraded one.

Config.Name: TAPE_API_KEYS
Config.Description: LEGACY shared-key auth, superseded by the per-service client registry (CLIENT_REGISTRY_ENABLED — now database-managed, set it via the admin API) and offered here only so an existing deployment can be read and retired. Comma-separated keys; when set, market endpoints require a matching X-API-Key header. Leave BLANK and use the client registry instead — a shared key cannot express scopes, so every holder gets the operator surface too.
